questions.question: He is known to me' is an example of -----[]
options: compound sentence
complex sentence
active voice
passive voice
questions.explanation:
“He is known to me” বাক্যটি Passive Voice। এখানে He হলো subject এবং is known হলো passive verb form (be + past participle)।
এই বাক্যের Active form হবে:
➡ I know him.
এখানে দেখা যাচ্ছে:
Active: I know him
Passive: He is known to me
Passive voice-এ সাধারণত object → subject হয়ে যায় এবং be + V3 (past participle) ব্যবহার হয়।

questions.question: Select the active structure.[]
options: The tree has been uprooted.
The door should be kept closed.
I have lost my watch.
My suggestion was not accepted.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, the subject "I" is performing the action. Options A, B, and D are in the passive voice.

questions.question: Tea is liked by common people' This is an example of -----[]
options: active voice
passive voice
quasi-passive voice
double-passive voice
questions.explanation: The subject "Tea" is receiving the action, and the sentence uses the "be + past participle" structure typical of the passive voice.

questions.question: The work is done by Medha' - This is an example of -----[]
options: active voice
passive voice
quasi-passive voice
None
questions.explanation: the work is the recipient of the action performed by Medha. It uses the "be + past participle" (is done)

questions.question: Rice sells cheap' is -----[]
options: Passive voice
Active voice
Both
None
questions.explanation: the verb "sells" is in its active form. However, it is a quasi-passive sentence because it has an active form but a passive meaning (rice does not sell itself; it is sold)

questions.question: "This school was built in 1971" is -----. []
options: past tense
past indefinite
passive
past perfect
questions.explanation: The school is the object that was acted upon, and the phrase "was built" is the past simple passive form.

questions.question: "All his pupils like him" বাক্যটির সঠিক Passive form হচ্ছে ---[]
options: He is liked by all his pupils.
He was liked by all his pupils.
He is like by all his pupils.
He is being liked by all his pupils.
questions.explanation: To convert to passive, the object (him) becomes the subject (He). Since the original sentence is in the simple present tense ("like"), the passive requires "is + liked" followed by the agent ("by all his pupils").

questions.question: "We read novels" passive form voice :[]
options: Novels is read by us.
Novels are read by us.
Novels is read by we.
Novels are being read by us.
questions.explanation: The object (Novels) is plural, so it requires the plural auxiliary verb "are" followed by the past participle "read". The subject "We" changes to its objective form "us" after "by".

questions.question: A race was run by him.[]
options: He run a race.
He ran a race.
He is to run a race.
He runs a race.
questions.explanation: The sentence "A race was run by him" is in the Passive Voice and uses the Past Simple tense ("was run"). To convert it back to the Active Voice, the agent ("him") becomes the subject ("He"), and the verb must remain in the Past Simple tense ("ran").

questions.question: A song was sung by Rupa.[]
options: Rupa was sung a song.
Rupa sings a song.
Rupa sang a song.
Rupa sung a song.
questions.explanation: this sentence is in the Passive Voice in the Past Simple tense ("was sung"). In the Active Voice, the agent ("Rupa") becomes the subject. The Past Simple form of the verb "sing" is "sang," making the correct active structure "Rupa sang a song."

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice of "BBC broadcast the breaking news".[]
options: The breaking news is broadcasted by BBC.
The breaking news were broadcasted by BBC.
The breaking news was broadcast by BBC.
The breaking news are broadcasted by BBC.
questions.explanation: The active sentence "BBC broadcast the breaking news" is in the Past Simple tense (note: "broadcast" is the same in present and past, but in this context, it refers to a completed event). To form the Passive Voice, the object ("The breaking news") becomes the subject. Since "news" is treated as singular, we use "was" + the past participle "broadcast" followed by the agent "by the BBC."

questions.question: We don't like idle people.[]
options: We are not liked by idle people.
Idle people are not like us.
Idle people are not liked by us.
Idle people are not of our liking.
questions.explanation: To change this simple present negative sentence to passive voice, the object (idle people) becomes the subject. Since "people" is plural, it takes "are not" followed by the past participle of the verb (liked) and the agent (by us).

questions.question: Fortune favours the brave.[]
options: The brave is favoured by fortune.
The brave was favoured by fortune.
The brave were favoured by fortune.
The brave are favoured by fortune.
questions.explanation: In the passive voice, the object (The brave) moves to the subject position. Adjectives used as nouns (like "the brave") are treated as plural, so they require the plural auxiliary verb "are" followed by the past participle (favoured).

questions.question: I don't like puffed rice.[]
options: Puffed rice not liked by me.
Puffed rice did not liked by me.
Puffed rice was not liked by me.
Puffed rice is not liked by me.
questions.explanation: The object (puffed rice) becomes the subject. Since it is an uncountable noun, it is treated as singular and takes the auxiliary verb "is" + not + the past participle (liked) followed by the agent (by me).

questions.question: Shirley paid the bill.[]
options: The bill was paid by Shirley.
The bill paid by Shirley.
The bill is being paid by Shirley.
The bill has been paid by Shirley.
questions.explanation: The active sentence is in the Past Simple tense ("paid"). To convert to passive, the object (The bill) becomes the subject, followed by the past singular auxiliary verb "was" and the past participle "paid."

questions.question: Cats kill mice.[]
options: Mice is killed by cats.
Mice are killed by cats.
Mice have been killed by cats.
Mice are being killed by cats.
questions.explanation: This sentence is in the Present Simple tense. The plural object (Mice) becomes the subject, requiring the plural auxiliary verb "are" and the past participle "killed."

questions.question: The city planner is making all the arrangements.[]
options: The all arrangements have been made by the city planner.
All arrangements are making by the city planner.
All arrangements had been making by the city planner.
All the arrangements are being made by the city planner.
questions.explanation: This is in the Present Continuous tense ("is making"). The passive form for continuous tenses must include "being." Since the new subject (all the arrangements) is plural, the structure becomes "are being" + the past participle "made."

questions.question: Mukti is writing a letter.[]
options: A letter is being written by Mukti.
A letter has been written by Mukti.
A letter was written by Mukti.
A letter has written by Mukti.
questions.explanation: This sentence is in the Present Continuous tense ("is writing"). To change it to passive voice, the object (A letter) becomes the subject, followed by "is being" and the past participle of the verb (written).

questions.question: The cheques are being signed by the manager.[]
options: The manager is signing the cheques.
The manager signed the cheques.
The manager was signing the cheques.
The manager has been signing the cheques.
questions.explanation: This is a Passive Voice sentence in the Present Continuous tense. To convert it back to Active Voice, the agent (the manager) becomes the subject, and the verb structure changes from "are being signed" to the active form "is signing" to match the singular subject.

questions.question: They are flying kites.[]
options: Kites are flown by them.
Kites are being flown by them.
Kites are being flowing by them.
Kites was being flown by them.
questions.explanation: This sentence is in the Present Continuous tense ("are flying"). To convert it to the passive voice, the object (Kites) becomes the subject, followed by the appropriate plural auxiliary "are being" and the past participle of "fly" (flown).

questions.question: I had written the letter.[]
options: The letter was written by me.
The letter had been written by me.
The letter was being written by me.
The letter was wrote by me.
questions.explanation: This sentence is in the Past Perfect tense ("had written"). The passive structure for the Past Perfect tense is "had been" + past participle. Therefore, the object (The letter) is followed by "had been written" and the agent (by me).

questions.question: Chapal has made tea.[]
options: Tea is being made by Chapal.
Tea has been made by Chapal.
Tea was being made by Chapal.
Tea have been made by Chapal.
questions.explanation: This sentence is in the Present Perfect tense ("has made"). The passive structure for the Present Perfect tense is "has/have been" + past participle. Since "Tea" is an uncountable, singular noun, it takes "has been made" followed by the agent (by Chapal).

questions.question: A storm has uprooted the tree.[]
options: The tree has been uprooted by a storm.
The tree is uprooted by a storm.
The tree has been uprooted for a storm.
The tree has uprooted himself.
questions.explanation: This sentence is in the Present Perfect tense ("has uprooted"). To change it to the passive voice, the object (the tree) becomes the subject, followed by the passive construction for the present perfect tense: "has been" + the past participle (uprooted) + the agent (by a storm).

questions.question: He has pulled down the curtain.[]
options: The curtain had been pulled down by him.
The curtain has down by him.
The curtain has been pulled down by him.
The curtain pulled down him.
questions.explanation: Similar to the previous question, this is in the Present Perfect tense ("has pulled down"). In the passive voice, the object (the curtain) becomes the subject. Because "the curtain" is singular, we use "has been" followed by the past participle (pulled down) and the agent in its objective pronoun form (by him).

questions.question: I had been doing the work for five days.[]
options: I had been done the work for five days.
The work had been done by me for five days.
The work had been being done by me for five days.
The work had been doing by me for five days.
questions.explanation: This sentence is in the Past Perfect Continuous tense ("had been doing"). The standard passive voice structure for this tense is "had been being" + past participle ("done").

questions.question: I shall do the work.[]
options: I shall be doing the work.
The work may be done by me.
The work will be done by me.
The work would be done by me.
questions.explanation: This is in the Simple Future tense. To convert to passive, the object (The work) becomes the subject. Since "the work" is third-person singular, "shall" changes to "will be" followed by the past participle of the verb (done).

questions.question: You will be helped by me.[]
options: I shall have helped you.
I shall helped you.
I shall help you.
I shall have helped you.
questions.explanation: This is a conversion from Passive to Active voice. The passive sentence is in the Simple Future tense. To make it active, the agent ("me") becomes the subject ("I"), and the verb changes to the active Simple Future form ("shall help").

questions.question: I shall be teaching him.[]
options: He shall be taught by me.
He will be taught by me.
He shall be being taught by me.
He will be being taught by me.
questions.explanation: This sentence is in the Future Continuous tense ("shall be teaching"). While standard English rarely uses the passive voice for the Future Continuous tense, the rule involves adding "being" to the passive construction. Thus, the object ("him") becomes the subject ("He"), and the verb becomes "will be being taught".

questions.question: We shall be taking tea.[]
options: Tea will be being taken by us.
Tea shall have been taken by us.
Tea shall be being taken by us.
Tea should be taken by us.
questions.explanation: this is a Future Continuous tense sentence. To form the passive voice, the object ("tea") becomes the subject, followed by the passive construction "will be being" + the past participle ("taken") + the agent ("by us").

questions.question: He killed himself.[]
options: Himself was killed by him.
Himself would be killed by him.
He was killed himself.
He was killed by himself.
questions.explanation: This is a reflexive sentence. In the passive voice for reflexive verbs, the subject ("He") remains the subject, and the passive structure "was killed" is followed by the reflexive pronoun used with the preposition "by" ("by himself") to indicate that the subject performed the action upon themselves.

questions.question: They love each other.[]
options: Each other are loved by them.
Each other were loved by them.
Each other loved by them.
They are loved by each other.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses the reciprocal pronoun "each other." When converting to the passive voice, the subject ("They") remains the subject, the verb "love" changes to the passive form "are loved," and the object phrase "by each other" is added.

questions.question: Lila fans herself.[]
options: Lila was fanned by herself.
Lila is fanned herself.
Herself is fanned by Lila.
Lila is fanned by herself.
questions.explanation: this is a reflexive sentence in the present tense ("fans"). To form the passive, the subject ("Lila") remains the subject, the verb changes to the passive present tense "is fanned," and the reflexive pronoun is added with the preposition "by" ("by herself").

questions.question: They married each other.[]
options: They were married by each other.
They got married.
They were married each other.
They had been married by each other.
questions.explanation: This sentence describes a reciprocal action. To convert it to the passive voice, the subject ("They") remains, and the verb "married" is converted to the passive past tense construction ("were married"), followed by the agent phrase "by each other".

questions.question: He has given me a book.[]
options: A book was given to me by him.
A book has been given to me by him.
A book has given to me by him.
A book had been given to me by him.
questions.explanation: This is a Present Perfect sentence with two objects (direct object: "a book"; indirect object: "me"). To form the passive voice, the direct object ("A book") is made the subject. The passive structure for Present Perfect is "has/have been" + past participle ("given"). Therefore, it becomes "A book has been given to me by him".

questions.question: He gave me a pen.[]
options: A pen was given to me by him.
A pen is given to me by him.
A pen was being given to me by him.
A pen is being given to me by him.
questions.explanation: This sentence is in the Past Simple tense ("gave"). When a sentence has two objects, you can make either one the subject in the passive voice. The verb "gave" becomes "was/were given".

questions.question: The cow gives us milk.[]
options: We are being given milk by the cow.
We are given milk by the cow.
Milk is given to us by the cow.
Milk is being given to us by the cow.
questions.explanation: This is a sentence with two objects (direct object: "milk"; indirect object: "us"). When the direct object ("Milk") becomes the subject in the passive voice, it requires the preposition "to" before the indirect object ("to us"). The verb "gives" (simple present) becomes "is given".

questions.question: The passive voice of 'He made us work is' -----[]
options: We was made the work by him.
Work was made by him for us.
Work were made by him to us.
We were made the work by him.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, the structure involves a causative verb. Converting "He made us work" into passive voice requires focusing on the work being done. The verb "made" (simple past) becomes "was made," and the agent "him" performs the action for the indirect object "us".

questions.question: He pleases us.[]
options: We are pleased by him.
We were pleased with him.
We are pleased with him.
We will be pleased by him.
questions.explanation: This is a special case in passive voice. Verbs expressing emotions, such as "please," "satisfy," or "disgust," are followed by the preposition "with" rather than "by" when converted to the passive voice. Therefore, "He pleases us" becomes "We are pleased with him".

questions.question: His behaviour surprised me. (Passive)[]
options: I surprised at his behaviour.
I was surprised with his behaviour.
I had been surprised at his behaviour.
I was surprised at his behaviour.
questions.explanation: When converting sentences with verbs like "surprise," "astonish," "alarm," or "disappoint" into the passive voice, we typically use the preposition "at" instead of "by". The past simple active "surprised" becomes the past simple passive "was surprised".

questions.question: The boy pleased us. (Passive)[]
options: We were pleased by the boy.
We were pleased at the boy.
We were pleased with the boy.
We were pleased to the boy.
questions.explanation: Similar to Q38, verbs expressing emotion or states of mind, such as "please," "satisfy," or "disgust," are followed by the preposition "with" when converted to the passive voice. Therefore, "pleased us" becomes "were pleased with".

questions.question: Which one is the correct passive form ?[]
options: I was charmed at her beauty.
I was charmed by her beauty.
I was charmed for her beauty.
I was charmed to her beauty.
questions.explanation: Similar to verbs like "surprise," verbs denoting states of mind or reactions (like "charm") often take specific prepositions other than "by" in the passive voice. Here, "at" is used to express the cause of the feeling.

questions.question: He annoyed me.(Passive)[]
options: I was annoyed by him.
I was annoyed at him.
I was annoyed with him.
I was annoyed against him.
questions.explanation: When someone is annoyed by a person, the preposition "with" is typically used in the passive construction (e.g., "I was annoyed with him").

questions.question: His conduct annoyed me.[]
options: He annoyed me with conduct.
I was annoyed with his conduct.
I was annoyed from his conduct.
I was annoyed at his conduct.
questions.explanation: While the options for this question are cut off in the image, the grammatical rule for being annoyed by an action or conduct usually involves the preposition "at" (e.g., "I was annoyed at his conduct"). However, if the provided quiz context follows the pattern of the previous question regarding the verb "annoyed," "with" may be the intended answer in this specific quiz, though "at" is often considered more standard for non-human causes.

questions.question: My teacher embodies all the good qualities.[]
options: All the good qualities are embodied by my teacher.
All the good qualities are embodied in my teacher.
All the good qualities are embodied to my teacher.
All the good qualities are embodied on my teacher.
questions.explanation: When converting to passive voice with the verb "embody," the preposition "in" is used rather than "by" to denote that these qualities reside within the person.

questions.question: Smoke fills the room.[]
options: The room is filled by smoke.
The room is filled in smoke.
The room is filled at smoke.
The room is filled with smoke.
questions.explanation: With the verb "fill," the preposition "with" is typically used in the passive voice (e.g., "The room is filled with smoke") to indicate what is causing it to be full, rather than "by".

questions.question: Do you know them ?[]
options: Is they know by you ?
Are they known to you ?
Are they know by you ?
Are they know with you ?
questions.explanation: The verb "know" is a special case in the passive voice. When converting a sentence with "know" to the passive voice, it is followed by the preposition "to" instead of "by". The sentence is in the simple present interrogative form, so the structure becomes "Are [object] + past participle + to [subject]?"

questions.question: His behaviour worried us.[]
options: We were worried about his behaviour.
We were worried with his behaviour.
We were worried by his behaviour.
We have been worried by his behaviour.
questions.explanation: Similar to other verbs expressing emotions or states (like "please" or "surprise"), the verb "worry" often takes a specific preposition in the passive voice. In this context, to express the cause of the worry, "about" is used to make the sentence grammatically natural.

questions.question: All of his friends laughed at him.[]
options: He laughed at all of his friends.
He was laughed at by all of his friends.
All his friends had laughed at him.
All his friends were laughed at him.
questions.explanation: This sentence contains a phrasal verb ("laughed at"). When converting to the passive voice, the preposition "at" must be retained along with the passive verb "was laughed." The object ("him") becomes the subject ("He"), followed by "was laughed at" and the agent ("by all of his friends").

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: A new cabinet has been sworn in in Dhaka.
A new cabinet has been sworn at Dhaka.
A new cabinet has been sworn by Dhaka.
A new cabinet has sworn in in Dhaka.
questions.explanation: This is a passive voice construction of the phrasal verb "swear in." The object ("A new cabinet") becomes the subject, followed by the passive perfect tense "has been" and the past participle "sworn in." The final "in" is part of the phrasal verb, and the second "in" is the preposition used for the location "Dhaka".

questions.question: Panic seized me.(Passive)[]
options: I was seized with panic.
I was being seized by panic.
I was seized by panic.
I was seized from panic.
questions.explanation: Similar to other verbs expressing emotions or sudden internal states, the verb "seize" in this context takes the preposition "with" instead of "by" when converted to the passive voice to describe the condition.
